[{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Model Monitoring, Drift Detection, and Retraining Pipelines"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"Deploying a machine learning model to production is only the beginning of its lifecycle. Over time, the real-world environment changes, causing the statistical properties of the input data and the target variable to evolve. This phenomenon, known as model degradation, necessitates a robust MLOps framework comprising model monitoring, drift detection, and automated retraining pipelines."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"Understanding Drift: Data Drift vs. Concept Drift"},{"order":4,"type":"paragraph","text":"Before building monitoring systems, it is crucial to distinguish between the two primary types of drift that impact predictive models in production:"},{"order":5,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Data Drift (Covariate Shift): Changes in the distribution of input features (P(X)) over time, while the conditional probability of the output given the input (P(Y|X)) remains unchanged."},{"order":6,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Concept Drift: Changes in the statistical relationship between the input features and the target variable (P(Y|X)), meaning the same input features now map to a different target."},{"order":7,"type":"subheading","text":"Implementing Statistical Drift Detection"},{"order":8,"type":"paragraph","text":"To detect data drift programmatically, we can compare a reference dataset (usually the training dataset) against a current production dataset using statistical tests such as the Kolmogorov-Smirnov (KS) test for numerical features or Population Stability Index (PSI)."},{"order":9,"type":"code","text":"import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
from scipy.stats import ks_2samp

def detect_ks_drift(reference_df, current_df, threshold=0.05):
    drift_results = {}
    for column in reference_df.select_dtypes(include=[np.number]).columns:
        stat, p_value = ks_2samp(reference_df[column], current_df[column])
        drift_detected = p_value < threshold
        drift_results[column] = {'p_value': p_value, 'drift_detected': drift_detected}
    return drift_results"},{"order":10,"type":"subheading","text":"Designing an Automated Retraining Pipeline"},{"order":11,"type":"paragraph","text":"When drift is detected beyond an acceptable threshold, the MLOps pipeline should automatically trigger a retraining sequence. This typically involves fetching fresh data, validating it, training the model, evaluating it against the current production champion model, and deploying it if performance improves."},{"order":12,"type":"code","text":"from sklearn.ensemble import RandomForestClassifier
from sklearn.metrics import accuracy_score

def retrain_and_evaluate(X_train, y_train, X_test, y_test, current_champion_model):
    new_model = RandomForestClassifier(random_state=42)
    new_model.fit(X_train, y_train)
    
    predictions = new_model.predict(X_test)
    new_accuracy = accuracy_score(y_test, predictions)
    
    champion_predictions = current_champion_model.predict(X_test)
    champion_accuracy = accuracy_score(y_test, champion_predictions)
    
    if new_accuracy > champion_accuracy:
        print('New model promoted to production.')
        return new_model
    else:
        print('Champion model retained.')
        return current_champion_model"},{"order":13,"type":"subheading","text":"Best Practices for Production MLOps"},{"order":14,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Log all prediction requests and responses securely for continuous offline analysis."},{"order":15,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Set up automated alerts (via Slack, PagerDuty, or email) when drift metrics exceed critical bounds."},{"order":16,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Implement circuit breakers or fallback mechanisms to handle pipeline failures gracefully."}]
